A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 52-page versions of the same work, including Appendices A–G. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that all material is comparable, with localized changes on six pages.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original logistic-regression convergence and timing experiments on MNIST and CIFAR-10. Appendix G.3 reports additional inversion-bias experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experiments in Section 5 and Appendix G.3, including the empirical results in Figures 2–4.

M1.justification: The sampling corrections, scalar debiasing procedures, and SSN updates are unchanged. The introductory formula corrections do not alter the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use MNIST and CIFAR-10 for the same binary logistic-regression and inversion-bias experiments. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Figures 2–3 retain the same comparisons involving Newton-LESS, GD, SGD, and the SSN sampling variants. Figure 4 retains RLev, ARLev, and DARLev, each with and without scalar debiasing.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix G retain the same preprocessing, sample dimensions, regularization, sketch sizes, iteration counts, metrics, step-size procedures, and timing accounting.

E4.justification: The sketch-size analysis in Figure 2 and the exact-versus-approximate sampling and debiasing comparisons in Appendix G.3/Figure 4 are unchanged. No additional ablation or robustness analysis appears.

E5.justification: Figures 2, 3, and 4 still report averaging over 30, 10, and 500 independent runs, respectively, with deterministic GD excepted in Figure 3. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Section 5 revises the qualitative speed comparison: v2 says SRHT closely competes with and slightly outpaces Newton-LESS; v3 says it outperforms Newton-LESS but trails all other SSN variants. This is a limited correction to the reported finding; all plotted results remain identical.

T1.justification: The introduction changes the Gaussian expected inverse from ((m/(m-d-1))A^T A)^(-1) to (m/(m-d-1))(A^T A)^(-1), with an analogous correction for the LESS factor m/(m-d). These change the scalar scaling. Theorems and appendix proofs are unchanged; moving deterministic factors outside expectations in Section 3 is mathematically equivalent.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about correcting sampling inversion bias and establishing problem-independent local convergence rates for SSN.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations, applicability boundaries, limitations, and future directions are unchanged. The Section 5 edit concerns an observed speed comparison, without adding an explanation or limitation.

D1.justification: Appendix G retains identical implementation details, preprocessing instructions, sampling constructions, regularization settings, and repository access information. No reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion, and novelty positioning are unchanged. Correcting the introductory formulas does not change the paper's stated relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized edits to the Section 5 comparison paragraph, adjusts expectation notation in Section 3, and updates the document date and arXiv stamp. Section order and the broader narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: All four figures retain identical plots, axes, legends, captions, and placement. The document retains the same page layout and appendix organization, with no added or reorganized visual displays.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects the reciprocal scaling errors in the introductory Gaussian and LESS bias formulas and makes the speed description more consistent with Figure 3. These improve mathematical accuracy and reporting clarity, while the method, theoretical guarantees, appendix proofs, and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
